whyItems.title: It compares access to purpose
whyItems.body: A flashlight needs a torch, not your messages. We check whether what an app asks for makes sense for what it claims to do.

whyItems.title: It detects repackaged apps
whyItems.body: A copied app can keep a trusted name while being signed by someone else. We check the signature.

whyItems.title: It tells you what to do next
whyItems.body: A score alone does not help. Every result comes with clear steps you can take right now.

patterns.title: Suspicious patterns
patterns.sub: These are combinations of access that appear together in known scams.
patterns.consequence: If this app is malicious, these permissions together could let it {consequence}.

otp_stealer.label: One-time password theft pattern
otp_stealer.body: This app can read your messages and also watch your notifications or control your screen. Together, that is how one-time passwords are stolen.

banking_trojan.label: Banking fraud pattern
banking_trojan.body: This app can draw over other apps, control your screen and read messages. That combination is used to show a fake bank screen and capture what you type.

spyware_profile.label: Spyware pattern
spyware_profile.body: This app can use your microphone, camera and location, and it starts by itself. It has no visible reason to need this.

dropper.label: Hidden app installer pattern
dropper.body: This app can install other apps without opening the app store. That is how unwanted apps get onto a phone.

device_admin_lock.label: Difficult to remove
device_admin_lock.body: This app can register as a device administrator, which can make it harder to uninstall.

call_intercept.label: Call interception pattern
call_intercept.body: This app can read your call history, place calls and use the microphone.

repackaged_signer.label: Different developer signature
repackaged_signer.body: The signature on this file does not match the official version of the app it claims to be.

steps.playbook.remove_if_installed: If you already installed {app}, remove it: open Settings, then Apps, then select it and choose Uninstall.
steps.playbook.contact_bank_if_otp: If you shared an OTP, a PIN or a password with anyone, contact your bank straight away using the number printed on your card.
steps.playbook.report_cybercrime: To report it, call 1930 or visit cybercrime.gov.in.
steps.playbook.dont_share_info: Do not send money, OTPs or personal documents to the sender.
steps.playbook.verify_officially: Check the claim on the organisation's official website or the number on your card, not through the link you were sent.
steps.playbook.review_permissions: If you decide to install it, allow only the permissions you understand and deny the rest.
steps.playbook.watch_for_ads: Watch for full-screen ads or unexpected pop-ups after installing. Remove the app if they appear.

apk.title: What is an APK?
apk.body: An APK is an Android app file, the kind you install on your phone. Apps from the Play Store arrive as APKs too, but you never see that step. When someone sends you an APK directly on WhatsApp, it did not go through the Play Store, so nobody has checked it.

permissions.title: What are permissions?
permissions.body: A permission is an app asking your phone for access — to your messages, your camera or your location. Android shows you a list when you install an app. Most people tap Allow without reading it, because the list is hard to understand.

sms.title: Why is SMS access sensitive?
sms.body: Your bank sends a one-time password by SMS when you make a payment. An app that can read your messages can read that code as it arrives, which is enough to complete a payment without your knowledge. A torch or a game has no reason to need it.

accessibility.title: What is accessibility access?
accessibility.body: Accessibility is a genuine feature built to help people who have difficulty using a touchscreen. It can also let an app read everything on your screen and press buttons for you. Because of that, it is one of the most misused permissions, and legitimate apps rarely need it.

repackaged.title: What is a repackaged app?
repackaged.body: A repackaged app is a real app that someone has taken apart, modified and rebuilt. It keeps the original name and icon so it looks familiar, but it is signed with a different key and can carry extra permissions. The app you trust is not the app you are installing.

safe.title: Can a check prove an app is safe?
safe.body: No. AppAutopsy reads what a file says about itself. It cannot see what the app will do once it runs. A low score means no warning signs appeared in the checks that ran — not that the app is harmless.
